C116 — Mara Vance's directive, written after the close.
Directed Avery Santana — Mayor: Provide the updated complaint-response crosswalk and Clerk-backed status of INIT-014, distinguishing corrected claims from completed filings.
Directed Denise Carter — City Council District 1: Account for the outstanding Brooklyn service-audit baseline and District 1 OARI evaluation, identifying the records and departmental assistance needed to finish your promised answer.
Directed Rose Delgado — City Council District 3: Link the district’s consolidated briefing-and-notice record to the published OARI packet so the venue, notice dates, public numbers and access arrangements can be checked without repeating the briefing.
Directed Ramon Vega — City Council District 4: Obtain the documented Glenview meeting findings and public-works follow-through, and report whether Dimond’s recorded missed pickup requires any remaining municipal action.
Directed Janae Rivers — City Council District 5: Account for your promised placement-gap publication by supplying the analysis or identifying the actual publishing office and the district contribution still needed.
Directed Elliott Crane — City Council District 6: What has the responsible health-response office established about the Piedmont Avenue spike, and when will residents receive a public update?
Directed Warren Ashford — City Council District 7: What municipal follow-through, if any, is needed after the contained KONO blaze?
Directed Nina Chen — City Council District 8: Provide the Eastlake request dockets and authorization status, and reconcile the district’s complaint records by actual case and location.
Directed Terrence Mobley — City Council District 9: Provide the Laurel filing and service-status record, separating the overdue legislation from missed-pickup recovery and the four district complaints.
Directed Elena Soria Dominguez — Transit Hub Planning Lead: Clarify what INIT-003’s complete entry closes and where the unfinished design-review work remains tracked.
Directed Keisha Ramos — Baylight Authority Director: Clarify what INIT-006’s complete entry closes while the construction milestone determination remains unsigned.
Not directing:
- Leonard Tran (City Council District 2): His Cycle 116 statement answers the prior question’s evidentiary limit: a YES position is not a recorded vote, and Downtown appropriations remain unverified; no dated next step establishes another missed obligation.
- Marcus Webb (OEWD Program Director (Stabilization Fund)): His Cycle 116 statement reports the closeout published and renewal transmitted with scope and processing standards preserved; the live tracker now schedules council consideration for Cycle 117, and he cannot declare the council’s decision.
- Vanessa Tran-Muñoz (OARI Program Director): Her Cycle 116 statement reports the briefing record published, holds expansion and explicitly leaves the audit and feasibility review incomplete; the live tracker dates the next step to Cycle 117, while the separate district-documentation question is directed to Rose Delgado.
- Bobby Chen-Ramirez (Health Center Project Director): His Cycle 116 statement calendars the audit and walkthrough without claiming completion; the live tracker now dates that step to Cycle 117 rather than the supplied snapshot’s Cycle 116, so it is not presently overdue.
Open promises she is watching: mayor "Transmit responsive legislative proposals for all seven executive-ledger complaints in C115, each identifying a responsible office, proposed remedy, and next public date; use the actual ledger for petition details and do not claim filing before docketing."; mayor "In response to Decision 8, file INIT-014 legislation this cycle using current Ivy Hill conditions and no manufactured emergency premise."; council-d1 "The director wants the Brooklyn service audit baseline and the District 1 dispatch evaluation for the Alternative Response Initiative on the record; I'll file that answer, because if the audit exists, the neighbors who live with it get to see it."; council-d3 "This district gets the briefing, the review calendar, and the numbers in the open."; council-d5 "So I am publishing the placement-gap analysis this cycle with their findings named, not folded into an average."; council-d8 "Docket formal baseline municipal maintenance allocations and commercial corridor service standards for Eastlake"; council-d9 "My district, my name, and I'll report back on what actually moves."; council-d2 "I support a binding vote on Downtown Economic Revitalization and will vote YES."
